title: Why Do Some People Have NO Wrist Tendon? 🖐️
description:
Touch your thumb to your pinky and bend your wrist: in most people a cord stands up in the middle of the wrist. It is the tendon of the palmaris longus, a small forearm muscle the body barely uses. About one person in seven has no palmaris longus, sometimes in just one arm (the share varies a lot between populations), and people without it grip just as hard. It probably helped our tree-climbing ancestors, whose forearms did more of the moving. Surgeons often take it out and use it to rebuild baseball pitchers' elbows (Tommy John surgery).
